review.finding: The trunk push compared only the end trees, not the guard's rule (ancestry, no merge commits, event-only commits). An amended release commit, a revert pair or a rebased history could publish a tag naming a commit not on the trunk. (Fixed in 08cb0c15e: one shared stdlib-only rule release_descent.py used by the hook and push-tag; real-git test over eight history shapes through both.)
base_branch was never written; the base fell back to origin/HEAD while the prose opens the PR with --base main. (Fixed: record-event records main; test with origin/HEAD different.)

A squash or rebase merge never makes the release commit an ancestor: waiting_for_merge forever. (Fixed: merged PR without the release commit is refused as merged_without_release_commit; closed PR as pr_closed_unmerged; guided squash tag repair stays a P8a follow-up.)
mode vs autonomy disagreed on when the tag waits. (Fixed: one key, mode; deviation from operator F1b for pipeline+guided recorded as D44 for stop 3.)
'no release commit recorded' was reported when only git failed. (Fixed.)
Subprocess-only coverage of the changed lines. (Fixed: in-process test.)
Pre-existing: release_guard.TRUNKS has master, release_event.TRUNKS does not. (Recorded, not built.)
